prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1325; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured driver, who is named on the policy. The claimant is not represented and reports neck and back strain.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and confirmed with the responding officer that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact. The other driver's statement matches the claimant's account of how the collision happened.

Entry 3: Two independent witnesses gave statements that agree with the sequence of events described by both drivers. Scene photos were received and reviewed.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle damage. The front-end damage is consistent with the impact described and with the speed reported. A few old scratches elsewhere on the body may predate this crash and have been noted separately.

Entry 5: Nothing in the records suggests the damage occurred before the policy coverage began. Coverage confirmed as in force on the date of loss.

Entry 6: Claimant contacted me and provided a few additional details about the collision, including where the vehicle was positioned after impact. The core account has not changed from the original report.

Entry 7: Reviewed the medical records. The reported neck and back strain is a plausible injury for a collision of this type. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history or the records obtained.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a usual course of physical therapy and follow-up visits. Symptoms have improved steadily and the frequency of treatment has tapered off as recovery progressed.

Entry 9: Asked the claimant whether any earlier neck or back complaints existed. The claimant denied prior issues, and no contrary records have been found to date.

Entry 10: Current assessment: the accident, vehicle damage, and reported injury are consistent with each other. Treatment is tapering as expected. File remains open pending final medical updates.
